title: Schmidt truncation, transfer operators and parent Hamiltonians

items.title: Finite open MPS and injective translation invariant tensor
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ and $d_1,\ldots,d_N,D_0,\ldots,D_N\ge1$ be integers. Give each site $j$ the Hilbert space $H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}$ with standard inner product $\langle x,y\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^{d_j}x_i\overline{y_i}$, linear in its first argument, and its fixed ordered standard basis $(|i_j\rangle)_{i_j=1}^{d_j}$. Tensor products use the ordered product basis and the product inner product. For every site and physical index choose a matrix $A_j^{i_j}\in M_{D_{j-1}\times D_j}(\mathbb C)$, a boundary column $\ell\in\mathbb C^{D_0}$, and a boundary column $r\in\mathbb C^{D_N}$. Here $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb C)$ is the space of $m$-by-$n$ complex matrices and $A^*$ denotes conjugate transpose. The associated finite open matrix product state (MPS) is the vector

$$|\psi_A\rangle:=\sum_{i_1=1}^{d_1}\cdots\sum_{i_N=1}^{d_N}\ell^*A_1^{i_1}\cdots A_N^{i_N}r\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_N\rangle\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N.$$

The dimensions $D_j$ are the bond dimensions; the virtual indices between adjacent matrices are matrix indices summed in their product. The zero vector is allowed. A nonzero vector is normalized by division by its norm, and normalization is defined only when $\langle\psi_A,\psi_A\rangle>0$. Every vector in $H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ has an exact open MPS representation for some choice of bond dimensions, with $D_0=D_N=1$ and $\ell=r=(1)$; the internal dimensions are chosen in the construction, rather than prescribed arbitrarily.

For a translation invariant tensor, let $d,D\ge1$ and use one family $A^i\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ for every site. Its transfer map is the completely positive linear map

$$\mathcal E:M_D(\mathbb C)\to M_D(\mathbb C),\qquad \mathcal E(X):=\sum_{i=1}^d A^iXA^{i*}.$$

Here complete positivity means that for every integer $q\ge1$, the amplified map $\operatorname{id}_{M_q}\otimes\mathcal E$ sends positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices; a matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian and has nonnegative quadratic form on every vector.

The tensor is injective at length $L\ge1$ when the matrices $A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L}$, over all $i_1,\ldots,i_L\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, span the full vector space $M_D(\mathbb C)$. No injectivity or transfer-spectrum condition is assumed by this definition.

For each block length $L\ge1$, define the blocked boundary map

$$\Gamma_L:M_D(\mathbb C)\to(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes L},\qquad \Gamma_L(X):=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_L=1}^d\operatorname{tr}(XA^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_L})\,|i_1\rangle\otimes\cdots\otimes|i_L\rangle,$$

where $\operatorname{tr}(Y):=\sum_{a=1}^D Y_{aa}$. Let $P_L$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, set $h_L:=I-P_L$, and, for $N\ge L$, define the open-chain parent Hamiltonian

$$H_{N,L}:=\sum_{j=1}^{N-L+1}I^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes h_L\otimes I^{\otimes(N-j-L+1)}.$$

For a positive semidefinite operator $K$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional inner-product space, define its ground energy by

$$E_0(K):=\inf\{\langle Kv,v\rangle:\|v\|=1\}.$$

A **ground-state vector** of $K$ is a nonzero vector $\psi$ with $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle/\|\psi\|^2=E_0(K)$. It is a **zero-energy ground-state vector** when $K\psi=0$; positivity then gives $E_0(K)=0$.

Each local term is positive semidefinite with kernel $\operatorname{im}\Gamma_L$, and $H_{N,L}$ annihilates every finite open MPS formed from the same translation invariant tensor. Every nonzero such vector is a zero-energy ground-state vector of $H_{N,L}$. This definition asserts no uniqueness of that ground state and no spectral-gap bound.

items.title: Transfer-generated infinite-chain state and correlations
items.statement:
Fix integers $d,D\ge1$ and a translation invariant tensor $A^1,\ldots,A^d\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ with transfer map $\mathcal E(X):=\sum_iA^iXA^{i*}$. A matrix is positive semidefinite when it is Hermitian with nonnegative quadratic form on every vector. Let $\rho,\ell\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ be positive semidefinite matrices satisfying

$$\operatorname{tr}\rho=1,\qquad \mathcal E(\rho)=\rho,\qquad \mathcal E^*(\ell)=\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1,$$

where $\mathcal E^*(Y):=\sum_iA^{i*}YA^i$, equivalently the trace-pairing adjoint determined by $\operatorname{tr}(Y\mathcal E(X))=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal E^*(Y)X)$. For a contiguous block of $k\ge1$ sites, write $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_k)$ for physical multi-indices, let $e_I$ be its ordered standard product basis, put $O_{I,J}:=\langle Oe_J,e_I\rangle$ for $O\in M_{d^k}(\mathbb C)$, and set $A^I:=A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_k}$. Define the transfer insertion map and local expectation by

$$\mathcal E_O(X):=\sum_{I,J}O_{I,J}A^JX(A^I)^*,\qquad \omega_k(O):=\operatorname{tr}(\ell\mathcal E_O(\rho)).$$

For any finite nonempty $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z$ and local observable $O\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, embed $O$ into the interval $[\min\Lambda,\max\Lambda]$ by inserting identities at missing sites and evaluate the same formula. For the empty region set $\omega_\varnothing(cI):=c$. These definitions give compatible positive normalized local functionals. Their unique density matrices $\rho_\Lambda$ obey $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$ whenever $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$. Assume Countable Choice. The transfer-generated infinite-chain state is the unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on the norm-completed quasi-local spin algebra whose restriction to every finite region is the defined local functional. No infinite tensor-product Hilbert space is selected.

For observables $O_A\in M_{d^a}(\mathbb C)$ and $O_B\in M_{d^b}(\mathbb C)$ on two fixed consecutive blocks, with $g\ge0$ identity sites between the blocks, the connected correlation is

$$\omega(O_A\otimes I^{\otimes g}\otimes O_B)-\omega(O_A)\omega(O_B).$$

items.title: Sequential Schmidt truncation
items.statement:
Input an integer $N\ge1$, nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_1,\ldots,H_N$ with fixed ordered orthonormal bases, a normalized vector $\psi\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ with exact coefficients in those bases, and integer rank caps $D_k\ge1$ for $1\le k<N$. For $N=1$ the cap list is empty. The algorithm performs the following exact finite procedure.

1. Set the current remainder to $\psi^{(0)}:=\psi$, the retained left space before the first cut to $S_0:=\mathbb C$, and an empty list of site tensors and discarded squared norms.

2. For each $k=1,\ldots,N-1$, reshape the current remainder as a matrix whose row index is the retained left index in $S_{k-1}$ together with the physical basis index in $H_k$, and whose column index is the ordered product basis of $H_{k+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$. Compute an exact singular value decomposition. Order the positive singular values nonincreasingly. Within each repeated positive singular value, form a deterministic orthonormal basis of its left singular subspace by projecting the row-coordinate standard basis vectors in lexicographic order and applying Gram–Schmidt, discarding zero residuals; obtain the corresponding right singular vector as $M^*u/s$ for singular value $s>0$. Retain the first $m_k:=\min(D_k,r_k)$ positive singular directions, where $r_k$ is the number of positive singular values, and record $\delta_k:=\sum_{j=m_k+1}^{r_k}s_{k,j}^2$ from this current unnormalized remainder. Reshape the retained left singular vectors into a site tensor $A_k^{i_k}$ with left index in $S_{k-1}$ and right index in $S_k:=\mathbb C^{m_k}$; pass the retained singular values times the adjoints of the retained right singular vectors as the next current remainder $\psi^{(k)}$. Since the input has norm one and $D_k\ge1$, every current remainder is nonzero and each $m_k\ge1$.

3. After the last cut, reshape the remaining array as the final site tensor $A_N^{i_N}$, use outer bond dimensions $D_0=D_N=1$ with scalar boundary columns $\ell=r=(1)$, and return the resulting unnormalized open MPS $\phi=\psi^{(N-1)}$, the list $(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_{N-1})$, and the bond dimensions $(m_1,\ldots,m_{N-1})$. For $N=1$, return $\phi=\psi$ and empty lists with the same scalar boundaries. If $\|\phi\|^2=0$, return a norm-zero flag and do not normalize. Otherwise an optional normalized copy is $\phi/\|\phi\|$; the returned $\phi$ and discarded norms always refer to the unnormalized sweep output.

All coefficients and SVDs are exact mathematical objects; no floating-point threshold is used. The tie rule fixes a choice even when a rank cap cuts through a degenerate singular-value subspace.

items.title: Finite sweep termination and computable norm error
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, let $H_j=\mathbb C^{d_j}$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with fixed ordered orthonormal bases, and let $\psi\in H_1\otimes\cdots\otimes H_N$ have norm one. For integer caps $D_k\ge1$ at cuts $1\le k<N$, run the exact sequential Schmidt truncation algorithm on $\psi$ and let $\phi$ be its unnormalized output and $\delta_k$ the discarded squared singular-value sum measured from the current unnormalized remainder at cut $k$. The sweep uses exactly $N-1$ SVDs and

$$\|\psi-\phi\|^2=\sum_{k=1}^{N-1}\delta_k.$$

In particular, $\|\psi-\phi\|^2\le\sum_k\delta_k$. This is a current-sweep error statement; the $\delta_k$ are not asserted to be the Schmidt tails of the original input at the same cuts. If $\psi$ is represented exactly as an open MPS with bond dimension $D_k$ at cut $k$, then its Schmidt rank at that cut is at most $D_k$, and the dimensionless von Neumann entropy in nats of the reduced density $\rho_{1\cdots k}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{k+1,\ldots,N}|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ satisfies

$$S(\rho_{1\cdots k})=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{1\cdots k}\log\rho_{1\cdots k})\le\log D_k,$$

with zero eigenvalues contributing $0\log0:=0$ and the natural logarithm convention.

items.title: Certified transfer gap gives exponential MPS clustering
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix integers $d,D\ge1$, matrices $A^i\in M_D(\mathbb C)$, and the transfer map $\mathcal E(X)=\sum_{i=1}^dA^iXA^{i*}$. Let $\rho,\ell\in M_D(\mathbb C)$ be Hermitian and satisfy $\langle\rho v,v\rangle>0$ and $\langle\ell v,v\rangle>0$ for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb C^D$, together with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, $\mathcal E(\rho)=\rho$, $\mathcal E^*(\ell)=\ell$, and $\operatorname{tr}(\ell\rho)=1$. Assume that $1$ is a root of multiplicity one of the characteristic polynomial of $\mathcal E$, and define

$$q:=\max\bigl(\{ |\lambda|: \lambda\in\sigma_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal E),\ \lambda\ne1\}\cup\{0\}\bigr)<1.$$

Let $a,b\ge1$ and fix local observables $O_A\in M_{d^a}(\mathbb C)$ and $O_B\in M_{d^b}(\mathbb C)$. For each integer $g\ge0$, place $O_A$ on sites $1,\ldots,a$, place $O_B$ on sites $a+g+1,\ldots,a+g+b$, and place identities on the $g$ intervening sites. The transfer-generated infinite-chain state determined by $A^i,\rho,\ell$ has connected correlation

$$C_g:=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\ell\,\mathcal E_{O_A}\mathcal E^g\mathcal E_{O_B}(\rho)\bigr)-\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\ell\,\mathcal E_{O_A}(\rho)\bigr)\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\ell\,\mathcal E_{O_B}(\rho)\bigr).$$

For every real $r$ with $q<r<1$, there is a finite constant $C=C(A,\rho,\ell,O_A,O_B,r)\ge0$, independent of $g$, such that $|C_g|\le Cr^g$ for every $g\ge0$. The multiplicity-one hypothesis is algebraic simplicity; no diagonalizability assumption is made.

items.title: GHZ transfer has persistent connected correlations
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Use the standard inner product on $\mathbb C^2$ and its ordered basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$. For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$, let $E_{ij}\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ have entry $1$ in row $i$, column $j$, and entry $0$ elsewhere, with rows and columns ordered $0,1$. For each integer $N\ge2$, index the factors cyclically modulo $N$ and let $A^0=|0\rangle\langle0|=E_{00}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $A^1=|1\rangle\langle1|=E_{11}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. The periodic trace contraction has amplitude $\operatorname{tr}(A^{i_1}\cdots A^{i_N})$ on basis vector $|i_1\cdots i_N\rangle$ and equals $|0^N\rangle+|1^N\rangle$; after normalization it is the GHZ vector $(|0^N\rangle+|1^N\rangle)/\sqrt2$. The transfer map fixes $E_{00}$ and $E_{11}$ and annihilates $E_{01}$ and $E_{10}$. With $\rho=I_2/2$ and $\ell=I_2$, the associated infinite transfer state has $\omega(Z_1)=0$ and $\omega(Z_1I^{\otimes g}Z_{g+2})=1$ for every integer gap $g\ge0$, where $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$ acts on one site. Thus its connected $Z$ correlation is exactly $1$ at every gap and does not decay.
